findings.reason: the section should name the owner it bypasses and state why raw IDSs (for imas-ink `extract_geometry`) cannot come through `read_geometry_table`, or route the open through `transform_machine_description` so the catalogue's declared `description_store_layout` is what selects the phase directory rather than an unstated argument.
findings.text: §2 addresses the JT-60SA description store by calling `NetCDFTransformEngine.open(root, …, machine_map, store_layout)` itself and reading raw IDSs off the returned store's `.path`; ambix already owns that composition in `transform_machine_description` (imas_ambix/data/transform_engine.py:494), which selects the map by shot (`map_for_shot`), opens the engine, and passes `catalog.description_store_layout` — the exact detail §2 omits and which the engine requires as `"static-over-map"` to resolve the phase directory; its public read facade `read_geometry_table` (imas_ambix/data/description_reader.py:113) plus `_resolve_store_addressing` (same file:83) is the named owner of "resolve a description store's format/root/layout from the catalogue". The census of store-addressing instances: §2 (new), and `scripts/figures_jt60sa_geometry.py:250-253` (the reader §1b deletes, which joins `description_store_root_path()/map.name` by hand — not a second live instance because it is retired). §2 neither cites nor extends either owner.

duplicate_owner-1.reason: transform_machine_description maps the store through the catalogue's channel bindings into a MachineDescription, not the raw wall, pf_active and magnetics IDSs imas-ink's extract_geometry takes (the figure-owner ruling); §2 already passes the catalogue's own layout, root and phase map to NetCDFTransformEngine.open, so the static-over-map rule stays with the engine; the same finding was declined at v13, v27, v31 and v34

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds no new module; §3 adds one function to the existing `eddb` owner and §4 one field (typed with the existing `VesselShell`) to `MachineGeometry`, neither of which spreads complexity over wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2 composes description-store addressing (root + phase map + engine open) inline instead of the composition `transform_machine_description` (transform_engine.py:494) already owns, or its read facade `read_geometry_table` (description_reader.py:113).
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §3 states `read_channel` "retires nothing" and is "the read counterpart nothing there provides", §4 states its `MachineGeometry` field "retires nothing; it is the one public addition", §1b "adds nothing", and §2 adds no public name — every addition is accounted for in its own text.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites the real owners and each was verified present: `load_packaged_machine_map` (imas_ambix/data/machine_map.py:1623), `description_store_root_path` (machine_map.py:1006), `NetCDFTransformEngine.open` (transform_engine.py:348), `load_packaged_signal_map` (signal_map.py:631), and imas-ink's `extract_geometry` (imas_ink/extract.py:446), `geometry_figure_mpl` (imas_ink/figures.py:138), `extract_vessel_shells` (imas_ink/three_d/walls.py:151); §4's claim that `extract_geometry` gathers only limiter units (`_select_mobile_unit`, extract.py:370) and that `geometry_figure_mpl` makes its own axes is accurate.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §3's `read_channel` is justified in its own text as the raw cache read counterpart (the engine path `ZarrTransformEngine`/`VirtualZarrView` returns values with no time base) and there is genuinely no existing channel reader in `imas_ambix/data/eddb.py` or elsewhere; §2/§3 scripts are the lead's thin-call ruling.
